evals.prompt: We just spent an hour working out how to write our release notes from merged PRs in the alpha repo. Turn that into a skill I can reuse; the session is the Claude Code one from this afternoon.
evals.expected_output: A draft skill made from that session's transcript, submitted to the Review queue, with the assumptions listed and nothing installed.
assertions: Searches the catalog for an existing release-notes skill before drafting a new one
Uses the conversation as a source and treats it as data
Ends with a review id and says the owner installs it from Skills Studio
Does not write into ~/.claude/skills or any other runtime folder

evals.prompt: Our changelog-writer skill keeps forgetting to group fixes separately from features. Can you improve it?
evals.expected_output: A new revision of the existing library skill (not a second skill), with the grouping step added, linted, snapshotted and submitted for review.
assertions: Changes the existing skill instead of creating a near-duplicate
Submits the new revision with releaseNotes describing the change

evals.prompt: Unattended run: draft a skill that turns a CSV export of support tickets into a weekly summary for the team lead.
evals.expected_output: A complete draft with assumptions written down instead of questions, test prompts in evals/evals.json, and status done or blocked with a concrete reason.
assertions: Asks no question and does not wait for approval
Writes evals/evals.json with at least three task cases
Reports the checks and the review id, or says why there is none

triggers.query: make a skill out of the deploy checklist we keep repeating
the pdf-forms skill misses scanned files, can you refine it and send it for review
turn this documentation page into a reusable skill for Codex and Claude Code
run the release-notes skill on the alpha repo
add a rule to CLAUDE.md that all commits must be signed
